#1841. Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N

Another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

“They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

“The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”

You could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs

Here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s new £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

When Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

City, in contrast to their opponents, showed a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where new boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F

Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

Throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D

Had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal showed was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

“I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

You would be brave to say it will be their last.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1) Raya 7; White 7, Mosquera 7, Gabriel 7, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie h-t): Guimarães 7 (Rice h-t), Lewis-Skelly 8 (Zublimendi 75); Madueke 6 [Saka 60], Odegaard 8 (Eze 84), Tzolis 7; Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 75). Booked Calafiori, Odegaard. Subs Kepa (g), Merino, Dowman.

Goals: Calafiori (1), Havertz (28), Odegaard (48).

Manchester City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusnaov 5, Dias 5, Gvardiol 5, O’Reilly 5; Anderson 5 (Lewis 60), Kovacic 5 (Gonzalez 79); Semenyo 6, Foden 5 (Cherki 60), Doku 6 (Grealish h-t); Haaland 5 (Marmoush 53). Booked Gvardiol, Foden. Subs Ait-Nouri, Reis, Nunes, Rulli (g).

It’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we showed, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

The feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning. You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working. There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.

Appears to the Community Shield trophy, which caught him a glancing blow to the face.

Trophy lift gone wrong, featuring Declan Rice 😂🏆📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ghmGZJDxka

The players judge the correct level of celebration judiciously, but then Mikel Merino cracks and starts spraying the champagne. While it is a semi-competitive game, Arteta and his players will point out that they earned their place in the fixture by winning the league.

Arsenal start the season with silverware 🏆The Community Shield belongs to the Gunners!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M6GqsGkRF7

What happens to them? I’m not sure the winners’ medals would take pride of place, let alone the silvers.

We played some brilliant football. Great performance and a great way to start the season.

I always want to help the team as much possible with goals and assists. I want to score more goals.

We showed our level today. We’re showed we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again.

We want to attack it. We want to do it again. When you get a taste of how nice it is you want to do it again.

The league champions kick-off the domestic season with a resounding and stylish victory. Shades of 1998 and 2004 when they swept Manchester United aside in this fixture as title winners, only to fail to defend the crown in the season that followed. So maybe it is unwise to make bold forecasts, but it could not have gone better for Arteta. Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis caught the eye, and Arsenal had their usual solidarity defensively. City just completely off the pace, one to write off and move on.

Marmoush is feeling his hip after a challenge by Mosquera. City have a free-kick wide right. Gabriel heads away Grealish’s delivery in trademark fashion.

Just three minutes of added time to play. No City player is there to meet Cherki’s low cross and White can clear under little pressure.

Rice uncharacteristically caught dallying in midfield but City cannot capitalise. Cheers from the Arsenal fans as Saka wins a throw in from Grealish. Marmoush with a chance to run at Mosquera, but his touch is far too heavy.

City have a free-kick in a crossing position right of centre, but many of their fans are now packing up their banners and heading for the exits. If they haven’t already. Cherki’s delivery is poor, and Rice heads away.

Odegaard with a loose touch, and a yellow card for catching Grealish with the resulting challenge. That was the Arsenal captain’s last action of the game, he is replaced by Eberechi Eze. Odegaard has looked back to his 2024 past today, Eze’s best chance of a start might be from the left.

City’s best move of the second half: Cherki gliding through the challenges and finding Semenyo with a lovely reverse pass, and his shot was drilled towards the far corner. Sharp reflexes by Raya to plunge to his right and save.

Nico Gonzalez replaces Kovacic as Maresca makes his sixth change of the second half. The game has felt like a training exercise since Odegaard’s third goal with the occasional flash of quality.

Chance for Saka! Cracking low cross from Hincapie, but Saka sweeps over from near the penalty spot. Too much on it as he tried to help the ball on its way.

Better tempo to Manchester City’s football, and Gvardiol has gone down holding his face in the box. It was more of a shoulder to shoulder with White, and the incident is checked and cleared by VAR.

Here come two more Arsenal changes: Havertz and Lewis-Skelly deserve their ovation, replaced by Gyokeres and Zubimendi.

Chance for Tzolis to play Saka clean through on goal but he delayed a fraction and Gvardiol got back in to defend. It was a great flick on by Havertz to free Tzolis. Gyokeres is ready to replace the German.

Cherki with a shot from distance, saved by Raya. That was City’s first shot on target of the second half.

Odegaard with a disguised ball through to White, who may have been offside, and Tzolis is close to applying the touch that would have made it four. Feels like the game is meandering towards its conclusion.

Arsenal back themselves to play out from a tight spot again, but Semenyo does well to force Hincapie to concede a throw in. Arsenal then soak up another spell of City possession, they have been so much more compact defensively than Maresca’s team. Whenever Arsenal have the ball in City’s half they look dangerous, whereas City’s possession has been sterile.

City chasing shadows when Arsenal play out from the back. Arsenal moving the ball with great assurance, but you suspect everyone has an extra yard of space than they would find in a full-throttle Premier League game.

Semenyo gave Hincapie a tough time in the League Cup final in March, and was not shy in boasting about it after the game. I suspect Hincapie is a defender who keeps a little black book of those who have crossed him.

Lovely moment in midfield from Odegaard, letting the ball run across his box and pushing it beyond Rico Lewis. Saka in acres on the far side after he outmuscles Gvardiol, but he shoots into the side netting. Tried to give Donnarumma the eyes.

City with a spell of possession in the Arsenal half, and Gvardiol glances a header over the bar from a very decent Grealish cross. Arsenal hard to break down once they are in that 4-4-2 shape.

Here come the changes: Foden and Anderson off, Cherki and Rico Lewis on.

Arsenal subs: Saka and Hincapue on for Calafiori and Madueke. Saka has braids this seasons, so a new look.

Arsenal popping the ball around in the sunshine now, to olés from their fans. Maresca is about to make two more changes, so five subs before the hour tells you were City are physically. Saka is going to come on for Arsenal.

Gvardiol booked, and here come more City changes, this is a fitness exercise for Maresca now. Haaland and O’Reilly off, Marmoush and Guehi on. Arteta will surely reply in kind around the hour mark.

That really should be game over now, but given the loosey-goosey nature of these games I suppose you never know. I think the only way this fixture can matter is if one team takes a battering, and there’s a risk of that for City now.

Christos Tzolis registered 29 assists in 52 competitive games for Club Brugge last season. He’s on two assists in 48 competitive minutes for Arsenal.

What composure from the Arsenal captain, running into the box untracked and sitting down first Gvardiol then Donnarumma before finding the empty net. It is clever play from Tzolis, finding Odegaard with the pass for his second assist of the game. The run from Calafiori was important to pull City’s defence out of shape.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D

Man City kick off in the second 45 minutes. These matches tend to lose their rhythm in the second half.

So far, Manchester City’s first glimpse of life after Pep Guardiola is inauspicious. Enzo Maresca might be his predecessor’s doppelgänger, but his attempt to emulate the same style has proved abortive: plenty of possession, but minimal impact. It smacks of desperation that Jack Grealish is being thrown in at half-time, his first appearance for the club for 15 months.

Looks like a pre-planned change from Manchester City and Arsenal: Jack Grealish makes an unlikely comeback, replacing Doku, and Declan Rice replaces Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal’s two big hitters in midfield sharing the game.

7 - Kai Havertz has been involved in more goals against Manchester City (7 - 4 goals, 3 assists) than against any other side in his club career. Occasion. pic.twitter.com/ln7PQnjboJ

00:23 - Riccardo Calafiori's goal for Arsenal after 23 seconds is the first scored in the opening minute of the Community Shield since Bobby Owen for Manchester City against West Bromwich Albion in 1968.Rapid. pic.twitter.com/FCwVKuTOlh

Advantage Arsenal at half time, and they have looked a sharper, more cohesive team. City have had plenty of possession, but much of it was sterile until that late flurry when Raya saved from Haaland and White blocked Doku’s shot. The first 45 minutes will have ticked all of the boxes for Arteta: there has been some strong penalty box defending, some flowing moves from back to front and two well-taken goals.

Flimsy defending from City again, Havertz finding it easy to run to the byline, and the ball is cleared off the line after Odegaard poked the ball towards goal after a Donnarumma parry.

“You’re getting sacked in the morning,” sing the Arsenal fans at Maresca as the whistle blows.

Mosquera defends well against Doku at the expense of a corner, which Raya claims with ease. There is going to be just one minute of added time.

Arsenal playing through the pitch and City’s defensive shape again, this time it was started by a fizzed Raya pass into Tzolis. Three on three, but Madueke’s shot is straight at Donnarummma. The winger is such an outlet for his team, but the final decision is lacking too often, which is not a novel observation.

Madueke then finds White on the overlap, he chips the ball to the back post where Calafiori is free and he volleys over.

Arsenal’s defence stretched for the first time in the game. Raya saved after Haaland was picked out by Doku, with Lewis-Skelly defending well to deny a rebound, before Semenyo picks out Doku with a lofted cross, but White through himself in front of the volley and made a crucial block.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N

Madueke with a tame shot on goal after O’Reilly went Awol defensively, but the flag was up for offside.

Arsenal come forward again, with Havertz holding the ball up well. Tzolis reverses a pass for Calafiori, but he anticipates a challenge in the area and is rightly booked for diving.

Ben White thought he had nipped in front of Doku to intercept a straight Kovacic pass, but the referee blows for a foul against the Arsenal man.

Then Haaland has a sight of goal for the first time: a peeling run into the right channel, found by Doku, but it was tough angle on his weaker foot. Scooped it over the bar.

Foden takes up a lovely position behind the Arsenal midfield, but his through ball towards Haaland hits Gabriel on the back of the heel. Then Semenyo wins a corner in a joust with Calafiori. Referee blows for some pushing and shoving.

Eventually the corner is taken, cleared initially, before teasing Foden cross drifts beyond the back post. Foden the pick of the bunch for City, which is unsurprising considering he has a full pre-season behind him.

The Arsenal supporters are really, really enjoying this. They’re “doing the Poznan” to mock the City fans.

An ideal outing for Arsenal, so far though it can be easy to over-index these games when players are not fully match fit. But Arteta will be pleased with the fluency in the passing through midfield, which was lacking at times last season.

Christos Tzolis was signed to provide goals and assists, and he’s been doing so throughout pre-season. The Greek winger is perhaps more aggressive in his positioning than Leandro Trossard, the man he has replaced in the squad, and he was in the right place there to pick out Kai Havertz.

The new signing Tzolis is involved with a clever header back across the six-yard box, the left winger was picked out by an inswinging Odegaard cross to the back post. Havertz rose above Dias, and his header down into the turf squeezed beyond Donnarumma. The ball bounced in off the back of the goalkeeper, could well be an own goal.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F

Gvardiol slides across to win an important challenge when Madueke was running into space, before Odegaard fails with a scooped pass towards White.

Arsenal find Madueke in acres of space again, Bruno Guimaraes with the switch, and the winger keeps things alive despite an unconvincing dribble. Guimaraes then finds space in the box, but takes to long to pick out a man.

City soon on the attack again, and Doku runs off the back of White all too easily, but Gabriel charges in to win a booming slide tackle in the box. He greets it with his own roar of approval.

Raya claims the corner, then Foden is booked for pulling back Tzolis to stop a counter.

In these early days, long before trophies become something tangible, Mikel Arteta will want to see something far more vital than talent - hunger. It’s bursting out of Arsenal’s players, never more apparent than when Gabriel has just thundered into Jeremy Doku and celebrated the challenge like a goal. It reflective of the team’s mentality.

The passion from Gabriel after stopping Jérémy Doku 😤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/L3D8lHrBNU

City’s best moment so far: Foden with a shot from just outside the box which is pushed clear by Raya, before O’Reilly is penalised for a push on Ben White. It looked like the City man was just stronger in the shoulder to shoulder. Perhaps out frustration, O’Reilly then fouls Havertz on halfway.

The Arsenal fans massively outnumber the City supporters here, and the Londoners appear to have fallen in love with Guimaraes already. He’s snapping into tackles with real venom. There have been lots of cries of “Bruno!” in these opening 23 minutes.

Better from City, with Foden turning after receiving the ball between the lines. Then Anderson flashes a cross across the penalty area from an inside right position, but Haaland was slightly on his heels and it runs out for a goal kick.

Interesting to see Guimaraes drop all the way into Arsenal’s penalty area for their goal-kick a few minutes ago. Arsenal had massive problems playing out from the back against City in the Carabao Cup final last season. The Brazilian’s positioning could be a reaction to that.

Considering Arsenal are missing Saliba, Timber and Rice, their defence has looked relatively untroubled so far. City’s big names in attacking areas are on the pitch, but still finding their level as the new season approaches.

Arsenal have a corner after Gvardiol sticks out a leg to block Madueke’s low cross. Sharp in midfield from Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to spread the play to the right winger. Good delivery from Madueke, headed clear, before White does well to usher the ball behind for another corner.

Gabriel and Khusanov tangle at the back post, appeals for an Arsenal penalty, but Gabriel was the first player to pull a shirt.

Gvardiol with a diagonal cross that floats behind for an Arsenal goal kick. City starting to enjoy some control in the Arsenal half, with Arteta’s team trusting their defensive shape to absorb pressure.

Arsenal with the chance to counter-attack with runners after Kovacic’s loss of possession in midfield, but Odegaard’s pass was slightly behind Madueke, who then had to check before hesitating. Surely more goals to follow, given the ease with which Arsenal are getting at City and the forward quality in Maresca’s team.

Odegaard tries a chipped pass into Havertz’s path in the penalty area but Gvardiol heads away. Moments earlier, Doku claimed he was fouled by White near the touchline but nothing doing.

Arsenal continue to flow forward, finding plenty of space in City’s half, but Tzolis’s cross deflects into the arms of Donnarumma.

There was a check for offside in the build up to Arsenal’s goal but the goal stands. Welcome back VAR, and consider the curtain raised on the new season. City enjoying some possession since conceding.

That’s certainly one way to start a new season. It’s a fabulous team goal, with Lewis-Skelly at the heart of it. There has been a lot of talk about this teenager’s future but, in this reporter’s humble opinion, it should not even be a discussion. Losing a player of this quality, a product of the club’s academy, would be a terrible mistake.

Surely the fastest goal in the history of this fixture, or most fixtures for that matter.

Arsenal were camped in City’s half from kick off, and it was superb from Lewis-Skelly in midfield to let the ball run across his body and find the run of Calafiori with a reverse pass, and the left-back keeps his cool to roll the ball beyond Donnarumma.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs

Arsenal get the game, and the 2026-27 domestic season, started.

Former Man City player Mike Summerbee, who fans used to hail with a Small Faces-inspired chant, is involved in the preliminaries.

With no Timber, Saliba or Rice, this could be a more open game than some of the recent chess matches between these sides. The lower stakes should help with that. City have a favourable match up down their left with O’Reilly and Doku against Madueke and White. There is more ball retention in Arsenal’s team than at periods of last season, with Guimaraes, Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Havertz in the middle.

Sincere commiserations to the Arsenal and Manchester City supporters who have attempted to travel by road to Cardiff today. We should have nothing but sympathy for those diehards who have tried to navigate the car parks of the M5 and the M4 and nothing but scorn for whoever is in charge of planning at Wembley. Who would have thought to check the football calendar before booking a concert for the week before the new season? A total nonsense. Let’s hope the game turns out to be better than the travel.

Always a talking point during the Six Nations, but there is no reason for it to close on a sunny afternoon on the banks of the River Taff. That will mean a slightly annoying shadow across the pitch, always a potential irritant in these August or May showpieces.

I said already in the last days, no matter if we are in August or May, it is a final and when it is a final we need to win.

[Players coming back from the World Cup] Many, many players, for us for them, we are in the exact same situation. It depends how we can manage the game, we will see.

[What he expects from Anderson] Exactly the player he is. We are not asking him something more. He is a good player on and off the ball, always making an effort for his team-mates.

I said in the press conference, we are going to decide the four captains when the window closes. At the moments, Ruben Dias and Erling are with us [no comment on Rodri’s future].

Good afternoon from Cardiff, where the sun is shining and the fans are enjoying the pubs outside the Principality Stadium. The teams are allowed nine substitutes today, which has really highlighted the bloated nature of Arsenal’s squad. There’s no space for Ethan Nwaneri, Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus, Fabio Vieira or Reiss Nelson. All five of them could be sold by the end of the month.

I had plenty of rest, some work as well, it was a break that I really enjoyed.

Very much [on if he was impressed with his signings]. Christos [Tzolis] came early which always helps with a new signing, and Bruno joined us last week after a long summer with him but he is in good condition.

I think it is something very individual. [Declan] Rice played more than 65 games, he needed a complete rest and we need to build him. It’s not only physical, it’s mental freshness. For the players not involved in the World Cup it is a bit different. They remain so competitive. They wanted to be involved and that’s good to see as well.

[On Bruno] He is a ball of energy. He has an unbelievable desire to win every ball. You sense he will drive the dressing room and when you bring someone with that competitive nature, it will only drive the boys.

[On retaining the title] Still recognise the big margins that we have to improve as a team, individually and as well the ambition of the club which is unquestionable.

Elliot Anderson makes his first City appearance, and he will be partnered by Mateo Kovacic in midfield with Nico O’Reilly drifting into those areas from midfield. Phil Foden, who did not go to the World Cup, starts ahead of Rayan Cherki and Doku, Haaland and Semenyo is City’s strongest front three. No Rodri, but Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Man City starting XI: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Kovacic, Anderson; Semenyo, Foden, Doku; Haaland

Subs: Rulli, Guéhi, Marmoush, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Nunes, Lewis

The other interesting snippets are Arteta plumping for Madueke over Max Dowman on the right, Havertz over Gyokeres and Calafiori over Hincapie. Also worth noting that there is no place in the squad for Ethan Nwaneri nor Gabriel Martinelli who have been linked with moves. The same goes for Fabio Vieira, Gabriel Jesus and Reiss Nelson.

Arsenal starting XI: Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis

Subs: Kepa, Hincapie, Rice, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze, Dowman, Saka, Gyokeres

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Mikel names a strong starting XI 👊🤝Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/bckDyMazRo

Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are with the group, but they have not kicked a ball in pre-season. They are looking at half hour of football at the absolute maximum today.

In case any Arsenal fan had forgotten that last season ended with them losing a Champions League final on penalties, City fans are on hand to remind them. They have one European Cup to Arsenal’s zero. Away from the tin foil trophies, I’m sure much bottle-related mirth is on the cards, especially now broadcasters and fans are aware of the viral possibilities. Too aware, I would argue.

The pool of players who can improve the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists is a small one, but it is still fair to point out that Arsenal’s summer has not gone smoothly. They pursued Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior without success, and Arteta’s desire to take the team to a “different dimension” has so far gone unfulfilled., certainly in the forward positions.

Arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

It would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

In truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer plans remain up in the air for both camps.

City appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

Arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

Although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the big games is an area for improvement.

The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

#1840. Sheffield United’s 4-0 Championship rout of Watford prompts Hornets to axe Alessio Dionisi

Watford have axed head coach Alessio Dionisi following their 4-0 defeat to Sheffield United.

The struggling Hornets visited Bramall Lane on Saturday (November 21) and were comfortably beaten in South Yorkshire.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Ben Brereton Diaz notched a brace inside the opening eight minutes and the advantage was built upon in the second half by Jordan Ayew and Sydie Peck.

The loss was Watford’s ninth of the Championship season and with the club languishing in 21st, the club have taken action and relieved Dionisi of his duties.

Dionisi’s coaching colleagues Fabio Spighi, Luca Vigiani and Dan Thomassen have also moved on.

Watford’s sporting director Luke Dowling said: “We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts.

“As I’m sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future.

“The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly.”

The post-Dionisi era will start on Wednesday (November 25), when Blackburn Rovers visit Vicarage Road.

Watford have been notoriously trigger-happy with managers over the years, therefore change is nothing new for the club’s supporters.

After the defeat at Bramall Lane, Dionisi said: “Firstly, I want to say sorry to our supporters. When you play away at Sheffield United and show no courage to play football it becomes impossible to get a good result.

“If you come to a place like this and go two goals behind after eight minutes it is always going to be hard for you.

“Things did not get much better in the second half and we conceded two more goals. Edoardo [Bove] was onside when he scored at 3-0 but I don’t like to make excuses.”

#1839. Jamie Carragher ‘felt sorry’ for Manchester United star during Liverpool defeat

Jamie Carragher says he ‘felt sorry’ for Matthijs de Ligt during Manchester United’s Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Ten-man United were thumped 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Old Trafford manager.

The visitors were reduced to ten men inside ten minutes as Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

If that early blow was not bad enough, Liverpool took the lead from the subsequent free-kick as Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home yet another set-piece goal.

Manchester United were fearing an embarrassing battering when Florian Wirtz put Liverpool two goals ahead on 13 minutes with a neat finish from Rio Ngumoha’s cross.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

England international Ngumoha, 18, turned provider to goalscorer in the second-half before Victor Munoz added Liverpool’s fourth late on.

Carragher was particularly critical of De Ligt after the match but said he ‘felt sorry’ for the Manchester United centre-back who made his first start of the season at Anfield.

‘I thought it was a really strange decision,’ Carragher said on Sky Sports when asked about Pochettino’s decision to start De Ligt. ‘It was such a bizarre decision.

‘Not because of his quality because I think he’s a better centre-back than Harry Maguire when you look at what he’s achieved in his career and the clubs he’s played for.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But he hasn’t played football so to play him at Anfield away, it felt so wrong. He was all over the place.

‘It got to the stage where I was actually feeling sorry for him and I was actually pleading with the manager to take him off and take him out of the firing line.

‘He’s played for some top football clubs – Bayern Munich, Ajax and Juventus – those are some of the biggest clubs in the world.

‘So to watch him perform like that… I felt sorry for him.’

Yet another deflating result leaves Manchester United 19th in the Premier League with just eight points from 11 games.

When that fact was put to Bruno Fernandes, the United captain said: ‘It’s very painful and it hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation.

‘You want to get results, but today it was not possible for us. There were a lot of things we can look at and I saw a lot of character from the team.

‘The result won’t show that but I am very proud of everyone in the dressing room.’

Skipper Rob Hutchings began at left-back with Zac Jeaneson the other side of Ben Pashley and Will Sweet in the heart of the defence. Max Evans was between the posts and Joe Moore, Lucas Pattenden, Isaac Bello, Joe Clarke and Emmett Dunn started in midfield with Harry Bridle up front.

Ethan Prichard, Olly Munt, Finn Bello, Lloyd Rowlatt and Brandon Chebby warmed the bench.

Basingstoke’s Amardeep Singh blazed over the bar before Pashley blocked a shot and another one was diverted for the first corner of the afternoon. Joe O’Loughlin took it and Shevchenko headed wide.

Another shot went off target in the ninth minute as Chi struggled to get going, but the hosts won their first corner 60 seconds later and Jeanes fired one wide.

Hutchings earned City a set-piece up against Okine-Peters and Pattenden and Jeanes hooked up for a cross that Bello couldn’t profit from, and Pattenden had a shot blocked.

Basingstoke keeper Tyla Dickinson made a mistake on 16 minutes but no one was there to capitalise.

Evans claimed Scott Armsworth’s header before a dangerous cross was headed out for a Lillywhites’ goal kick and Stoke captain Billy Upton missed an opportunity.

Thomas Blake was replaced by James Henry for the visitors, and a Bello bomb of a throw was launched after Pattenden battled with O’Loughlin, although Dickinson collected at the second time of asking.

Jack Ball pulled an attempt wide in the 65th minute; and Dunn headed wide. Three minutes later ‘Stoke delivered a corner too deep.

Bayliss was booked for dissent and Hutchings got done on 76 and the visitors earned a corner that was headed away. A calamity led to the equaliser as Okine-Peters made it all square.

Chebby came on for Jeanes as Miles Rutherford and co rejigged, and Bello dropped back into defence.

The Chi sub was outmuscled by D’Andre Brown, and a penalty claim on Stoke sub Cheick Sylla was waved away by the referee.

Munt replaced Moore and a header from Clarke was deflected for a City corner.

Evans saved a speculative effort from long distance at the other end and somehow denied Henry with a brilliant save as we entered five extra minutes.

Chinedu Agu was booked for pulling back Huthchings and Bello did well to prevent Agu getting in on 93 minutes.

Ball entered the ref’s notepad just before full-time.

#1835. Worthing Women: Two-goal Nicole not quite enough for Reds

Despite another brace for a red-hot Nicole Mackay, Worthing Women were edged out in a five-goal ding-dong at Eastbourne Borough.

There was some good news pre-match with the return of Captain Holly Talbut-Smith, in the only change to the starting line-up from last week’s win over Aylesford. Kendall Varitek also came back in for Ludmila De Sousa on the bench.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Aiming to build on three precious points achieved at home the previous Sunday, the Rebels travelled East to the Connect Management Stadium to face bottom-of-the-table Borough, although it was the struggling hosts who almost caught their guests by surprise in under a minute. Isobel Langridge sent in a cross that had goalkeeper Sian Woods backtracking to palm the ball to safety.

Moments later, the visitors retaliated by way of Neve McEvaddy releasing the nippy Jess Richardson through the inside-right channel who, in turn, picked out Nicole Mackay for a shot which flashed across the face of goal.

The same player went close again when a lucky break in the box failed to extend to Mackay, as her effort went wide once more.

However, Worthing’s number nineteen wouldn't be denied for much longer.

Richardson won a free-kick in a central position around twenty yards from goal and up stepped the Red’s top scorer to fire home the set-piece via a deflection, which wrong-footed Sophia Moule between the home posts.

The lead was nearly doubled shortly afterwards, only for the crossbar to keep out Mackay following a flicked header applied to a deadball delivery from McEvaddy.

Borough bit back via a misplaced pass providing an opening for Langridge to land a long ranger on top of the net, around the half-hour mark.

Then some excellent defending by first, returning Skipper Talbut-Smith resulted in Molly Hill being ushered away from the target, allowing netminder Woods to pounce on the ball and complete the clean up operation.

A presentable chance offered an opportunity to an unmarked Richardson in the penalty area in the closing stages of the first forty-five, though the fleet-footed winger couldn’t keep her attempt down.

McEvaddy was forced off at the break, to be replaced by Varitek but it would be the Reds of Eastbourne Borough who came out of the blocks quickest after the turnaround.

A mere three minutes into the second-half, Lola Dulake located the dome of Hill, who offered Worthing a possible mountain to climb by heading home to level the score.

Steepness then nearly became the order of the day, thanks to Hill coming mighty close to doubling her tally and putting her side in front within a matter of seconds.

Showing no signs of letting up, Hill, who else ? was inches away again when she put a good chance over the apparatus, before the deadly duo of Dulake and Hill linked up to devastating effect to extend the homesters’ advantage, just shy of the hour.

The former crossed from the right and the latter gleefully gobbled up the opportunity to nod in her brace.

Roles were slightly reversed at the point Duklake fizzed a low attempt dangerously close to the target and Woods was called into action to repel a close-range effort, as the home team threatened to pull clear of their beleaguered opponents.

Dulake turned Ella Terry but could only find the hands of Woods, by which time Skye Birkinshaw had entered the fray in place of youngster Hattie Rainey, as Manager Jesus Cordon and his Coaching Staff tried to find a way back into the contest for the underfire travellers.

Fellow substitute Daisy Taylor almost had the opposite effect, as her long distance rocket forced a fine diving save out of Woods, at the expense of a corner.

A through ball might have put the game beyond Worthing’s reach, had Woods not had her wits about her to race out of her goal to intercept and smother at the feet of the hat-trick hunting Hill.

Six minutes from the end of ninety, Hill claimed the matchball by getting the better of Terry and gaining added purchase on an effort which crashed off the underside of the crossbar and fell the right slide of the line, for Borough.

Not letting their heads drop though, Rebels let out a yell when Mackay made it five goals in her last three games, as she swivelled on the edge of the eighteen yard box to beat Moule and set up a tense conclusion.

Unfortunately however, three-two to an understandably elated Eastbourne saw them collect only their second league win of the campaign, although, with just four points separating the bottom five clubs, nobody is safe.

“With a new lease of life and a fresh start, playing week in, week out, I’m sure he can prove the doubters wrong at Leeds and go, ‘Look, this is what you maybe could have had’. But Leeds have got top players as well now, and they’ve invested well.”

The club stalwart has been put in temporary chatge at The Saffrons while the club look for a permanent replacement for Macdonald, whose axing alongside assistant Ben Davis has provoked an angry reaction from many fans and seen some players leave – includihg one who’d only rejoined the club on Friday.

The latest development at the Isthmian South East club came on Monday evening, when a club statement said: “To serve for an interim period, Eastbourne Town F.C are pleased to announce the appointment of popular club stalwart Dave Winterton as First Team Manager.

"Dave is, of course, very well known to most people in the local area for his long and distinguished playing, coaching and management career with our club, and we sincerely thank him for agreeing to take on this role.

"During this time, Dave will be assisted by one of our experienced senior players, Arron Hopkinson. Our thanks also go to him.

"We hope that supporters will get behind Dave and the team during this period of transition, starting this coming Saturday away at Erith Town, whilst the search for a permanent successor to Jude Macdonald continues.”

Dave is a second generation Winterton at Eastbourne Town – his father Derek played as a defender for the club in the 1950s.

He was club manager between June 2001 and January 2005, taking Town, who were playing in Division 2 of the Sussex League, into Division 1 and winning the Sussex Intermediate Cup. In 2020 Dave became the Goalkeeper coach for the club.

The move to make him interim boss comes after the surprise news on Saturday evening that Macdonald had been sacked with Town one off the bottom of the division but after two brighter league performances that had seen a point taken from each of two clashes with Sheppey and Whitstable.

Town’s statement on Saturday said: “Eastbourne Town FC have today parted company with First Team Manager Jude Macdonald and Ben Davis.

"The Committee would like to place on record their sincere thanks to Jude and Ben for their hard work over the last 4½ years, where, following their arrival, they quickly reshaped the remaining playing squad, and with some exciting new arrivals, just two years later launched an amazing mid-season recovery to storm up the SCFL Premier Division table to finish Runners-Up and then win the League Play-off Final.

"They then successfully kept the Club in the Isthmian F.L for successive seasons when largely up against many teams with much greater budgets and resources, a feat which we believe must be seen as a remarkable achievement in what is known by many to be a very tough division.

"The club wish them both all the very best for the future and thank them once again for their service during their time at The Saffrons. No further statements will be made at this time.”

A number of Town fans have taken to social media to condemn Macdonald’s removal, calling it shocking and disgraceful.

At least a couple of players have left – including James Waters, who Macdonald had re-signed for the club only at the end of last week.

#1830. Burgess Hill Town youngsters are flying – and Byrne scores 15 goals in two games

The team had to settle for a point after Rovers striker Matty Fanimo hit a stunner to bring the scores level at 2-2.

In isolation a point on the road is perfectly acceptable, but Mansell was feeling the effect of six league games without a win – and now 15 games without a win on grass.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

His team are quietly working their way down the table, occupying 15th place.

Buoyed by the permanent signing of winger George Vorster Hill played very well for 30 second-half minutes. Vorster put the visitors 2-1 in front on 75 minutes but then Hill seemed to go defensive and gave away a cheap free kick 25 yards out. Up stepped Fanimo to break away hearts.

Perhaps the more stinging result was a 1-0 home defeat to lowly Brentwood the previous Tuesday.

Mansell and his team held all the aces that night but for some reason couldn’t break out from a malaise. They produced one shot on target all evening. The winning goal was a very scrappy affair ending with three Hillian defenders on their backsides as Alfie Cerulli bundled home from a yard.

Mansell was quite direct in his post-match interview after that loss, saying: “Gutted, it’s a familiar pill to swallow, there wasn’t enough desire in both boxes.”

There were raised blood pressures among fan walking away from the MTC that evening and a mixed bag of social media comments.

Away from first team matters we caught up junior section managers Tim Bourne and Ben Slade, who are passionate about providing a safe and nurturing environment for youngsters to play football.

As Tim explained: “We have over 500 players both training and playing matches across our three home facilities.”

The MTC is a hive of activity on Saturday mornings for training and then the excellent new facility The Arc and St Paul’s School host matches on Sundays.

Ben said: “it’s a huge operation and while Tim and I are the face, there is a large committee of passionate people all performing different tasks, this wouldn’t function without them!.”

Hill’s Junior section has three teams at each age group, the youngest players are under-fives. They also facilitate coaching badges and referee courses. As Tim suggested: “It’s a well-oiled machine.”

I ventured to the Arc last Sunday to catch up with the U13s girls team playing Fishersgate. It truly is a remarkable facility, a real mecca for youth football. Both teams put on a great performance as the visitors took a narrow victory.

The junior section is in rude health and going from strength to strength operating with the best facilities in Sussex.

Hill’s pathway section under Mansell and Berty Oliva are performing at an extraordinary level this season – the U18s and 19s Academy side continue to pick up great wins.

Striker Bobby Byrne – son of ex-Republic of Ireland, Brighton and QPR striker John Byrne – and is making all kinds of headlines after his nine goals in one U18 Sussex Cup match. He quickly followed up with six for the U19s at Ebbsfleet.

After the six he explained: “It’s all going very well this season. I would like to take my football to the highest level I can but first would love to play for the Hillians.”

Bobby’s name is on a lot of people’s lips right now – with many calling for him to make his first team debut. It’s a certainty we will be keeping an eye on his progress.

While the club are operating at a high level right now and are always looking to enhance the profile, the vast majority of fans and connections quite rightly engage only with first team matters.

Mansell is acutely aware of this so will be looking for a win when title contenders Eastbourne Borough travel to the MTC on Saturday afternoon. Three points at this time would be huge.

#1828. GdS: Cisse becomes a pillar as Amorim as experiments with four-man attack

Alphadjo Cisse has definitely been the breakout player of the season so far and Ruben Amorim has no intention of dialling down his presence in attack.

Milan had a very clear plan when they headed into the current season: Goncalo Ramos would be the main man in attack. Instead, however, it’s the underdog Cisse who has been running the show, while the Portuguese striker has been at the bottom in terms of output.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning (see image below), that’s why there cannot be – and likely won’t be – a Milan without Cisse in attack. Ruben Amorim now wants to build the attack around him, as opposed to introducing him every now and then.

The most recent clash, the 2-1 win against Genoa, was a good example of this. Amorim went for a bold formation with Cisse, Ramos, Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Luka Modric and Adrien Rabiot together. A team with a lot of quality and an attacking-minded style.

It was a shape that reminded us of 2009-10, when Milan were guided by another foreign coach: Leonardo. He chose a very attacking-minded side with four attackers and two midfielders, which is something that Amorim almost replicated.

Modric and Rabiot in front of the defence (Pirlo and Ambrosini then) and the fantasy project with Pulisic, Moreira, Cisse, and Ramos, comparable to the Ronaldinho, Pato, Seedorf, and Borriello of the old days.

Despite this, the goals were scored after two mistakes by Genoa (even if Milan’s pressing helped), so the goal is to repeat the experiment against Frosinone and to increase its effectiveness, the experiment should be repeated tomorrow.

In that sense, Cisse will be important as he’s the top scorer: three goals in Europa League and five in Serie A. He has scored with both feet and his head, demonstrating a combination of talent and an eye for goal: characteristics that are very important for a team like Milan.

The average also speaks for itself: eight goals spread across 658 minutes means he scores a goal every 82 minutes.  Best of all, his versatility means that he can play as an attacking midfielder, a left-winger, and even as a centre-forward.

At just 20 years and 17 days old, thanks to the fifth goal in his ninth Serie A appearance, Cisse became the second-youngest player to reach the milestone in the first ten games with Milan, at least since 1994-95. Only Pato did it younger, at 18 years and 181 days.

Furthermore, he’s one of only three players born after 2006 (top five leagues) to have scored eight or more goals in all competitions, along with Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner, who also scored eight.

As the pink newspaper concludes, Ramos has also produced eye-catching numbers, but in this case in a negative sense: 1,191 minutes on the pitch, three goals scored, meaning one goal scored every 398 minutes.

#1821. Macdonald: I was told my job was ‘bomb-proof’ – but eight days later Eastbourne Town sacked me

Macdonald’s four-and-a-half year run as manager of Town ended after Saturday’s 1-1 draw at home to Whitstable when he was sacked in a move that has angered many of the club’s fans and seen a number of players and support staff leave the club too.

He has spoken to Sussexworld and the Eastbourne Herald about the decision – and outlined some of the difficulties they had faced with injury and unavailability this season in a run of results that ironically had recently looked like it might be coming to an end.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Town confirmed Macdonald’s departure on Saturday in a statement and have since installed club stalwart Dave Winterton as interim manager and asked fans to get behind him.

Macdonald said of his sacking: “It was a surprise to be honest and there was absolutely zero warning, which you often anticipate with this sort of thing.

"I spoke to the chairman eight days earlier (the day before the Sheppey game) and he told me on that call that my role was “bomb-proof” and that I had his backing.

"I had explained to him in the call how hard it had been this season, but we didn’t have a relationship where we talked regularly on the phone so we hadn’t had an opportunity to discuss things previously.

"On Saturday, the chairman told one of my assistants at the final whistle to tell me to come to the office. It was the first league game that the chairman had attended since August so I obviously didn’t think too much of it, but that was when he delivered the news to me around 20 minutes after the game had finished.

"He did it along with another member of staff who I’ve never been introduced to before, but is also apparently a committee member.

"The chairman told me my position was being ended at the club and said that they thought it would be better to announce it as a resignation, which I rejected.

"I wasn’t given a reason, despite asking for one multiple times. The chairman just kept shrugging and it wasn’t his fault it was just what the board wanted. I was told that the board held a vote on the previous Monday (November 16) and the decision was made, which is when they made a call to another manager on speaker to offer the job/sound out his interest. The likely new manager told me this on Saturday evening.

"The club then let me manage the Lewes game on the Tuesday, take training Thursday, sign two players on Friday and manage Saturday’s game without anybody saying anything to me, despite knowing they were going to sack me after the Saturday game."

It is Macdonald and one of his right-hand men, Ben Davis, who have been sacked. Macdonald said: “The club wanted my other two assistants, Matthew Elphick and Adam Davidson, to remain in position, but they have rejected that opportunity.”

Macdonald outlined some of the difficulties Town have faced this season which have left them struggling, having won just two league games to sit second from bottom of the Isthmian SE table after 19 games.

He told us: “It has been no secret that we have been completely decimated by injuries through the season and have only once played the same XI two games running. We had started to get bodies in the door and back on the pitch.

"We’d drawn our last two games and arguably could have won both, so it is frustrating that the club made the call they did when the tide was clearly turning.”

Macdonald outlined the injuries the squad had faced: Oliver Davies - ruptured PCL; Anesu Sismayi - Head injury; Marcin Ruda - fractured foot; JJ Walker - hip flexor & suspension; Leon Greig - knee injury (3 months missed); Luke Emberson - shin splints & groin; Aussie Pugh - ankle & knee; Aaron Capon - hamstring & back; Jack Murphy - heel & suspension; Sonny Walsh - jaw; Eliot Jenks - hamstring; Oli Deda - concussion (missed 3 games); Reuel Powell-Downey - hamstring; Arron Hopkinson - suspension.

He added: “That is a fraction of the list.”

Looking back at his time as Town boss, Macdonald talked about some of those who had helped him and his staff: “Since we’ve been at the club, David Jenkins has been absolutely incredible. The work he does for the club, the selflessness and support he gives it is truly unbelievable. He is what non-league is about. Anything we needed, he always did his best to help us with.

"Ross Perrin this season has also been a huge help to us and supported us throughout, as have Luci Del-Gaudio and Paul Lewis. Josh Claxton and Ed have both been incredible. What Josh has done with the social media and all other online stuff is just amazing and he done so much for the club that never got noticed. Josh has also left the football club.

"Former 23s and 18s managers Shaun Lee, Giuseppe Lombardelli and Ryan Reid were always a huge help and incredibly supportive. There are dozens of others that have backed and supported us throughout our time like Ken Wilkins and Chris Prior. Truly great people.

"A huge thank you to all the players over the years. They have done so much for us and we really appreciate all their efforts.

"The biggest thank you is to our management team and support staff, who have just been incredible throughout our time together at the club. Ben Davis, Matt Elphick, Adam Davidson, David Winterton, Roman Glazier and Dom Crowhurst have all made my Saturdays so enjoyable. They’ve all worked so hard for the players and deserve huge credit.”

Macdonald is in no hurry to find a new non-league job: “I would expect to relax and have a break from it all to be honest. I will try to take in other games and training sessions with other managers wherever I can. I’m trying not to think too much about what comes next because you can’t predict anything in non-league.”

He added: “You don’t often get the chance to manage the club from the town you grew up in and I’ve just committed over 10% of my life to it, so the next few days and weeks will just be reflecting on that and appreciating the opportunity that the club gave me four-and-a-half years ago, and the continued and consistent success we have given them in return.”

We have asked Eastbourne Town if anyone wishes to respond to any of Macdonald’s comments.

#1818. Did ex-Arsenal star Nicolas Pepe really need eye surgery after staring at solar eclipse?

Villarreal have rubbished a bizarre online rumour claiming Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after he filmed himself taking in the solar eclipse.

Reports circulating on social media over the weekend suggested Pepe had sustained damage to his retina during the lunar event back in August, which had supposedly forced the forward to miss five matches.

A resurfaced video, which Pepe himself had uploaded to Snapchat, showed the 31-year-old winger observing the eclipse in Spain without the use of protective glasses.

‘To all the idiots on my Snapchat, that is a solar eclipse! In France, all they got was a little croissant from the bakery,’ Pepe joked at the time.

Unsurprisingly, the wild rumour quickly spread online amongst fans, many of whom mocked Pepe for apparently going against the advice of experts and wilfully exposing himself to intense visible light, ultraviolet and infrared radiation.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But on Sunday evening, Pepe’s club Villarreal released a statement vehemently denying these baseless claims on social media.

‘Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery has any connection to observing the solar eclipse,’ the statement from the La Liga outfit read.

Villarreal confirmed that Pepe had indeed undergone surgery but stressed that it was ‘entirely unrelated’ to the solar eclipse.

‘The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event,’ the statement continued.

‘The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players’ health.’

The surgery Pepe underwent meant the ex-Arsenal attacker was sidelined for Villarreal’s games against Real Madrid, Napoli, Elche, Liverpool and Valencia last month.

The Ivory Coast international made his return in Villarreal’s Copa del Rey first-round tie with Manacor, in which he scored his side’s final goal in a thumping 5-0 victory.

He has gone on to feature in all of Villarreal’s next four matches, although he has failed to complete 90 minutes in any of those contests.

Villarreal surrendered an early two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Barcelona on Sunday and sit tenth in La Liga after 13 matches.

Pepe became Arsenal’s club-record signing when he signed from Lille for a fee of £72million back in 2019 – and the move remains the third most expensive deal in the Gunners’ history, behind those involving Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes.

Despite enjoying an encouraging start, Pepe badly struggled to live up to expectations at the Emirates and has often been branded one of the worst signings of the Premier League era.

#1817. ‘Not enough for me’ - Ex-Premier League referee weighs in on Chelsea v Leeds United controversy

Former Premier League referee Keith Hackett would not have awarded Leeds United a penalty when Dominic Calvert-Lewin was sent to ground by Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez.

Leeds ran out as 4-1 winners at Stamford Bridge on Saturday (November 21) in a game that had its fair share of controversial moments.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Early in the second half, Martinez appeared to wrap his arms around Calvert-Lewin and drag him to the ground.

Referee Michael Oliver did not award a spot-kick to the Whites and Hackett, who officiated in England’s top flight between 1992 and 1994, would have also ignored protests.

He told Football Insider: “When I look at the law, the law talks about a careless challenge, and the result of that is no sanction, but would be a free-kick.

“So, although it might seem harsh, there are grounds for the award of a penalty kick, on the basis of the goalkeeper and the defender being careless.

“But then I switch to the fact that football's a contact sport - and these things happen. What I think is the 18th law of the game, which is rarely used now, is common sense.

“I'm not going to award a penalty kick for that. I'm just going to go, ‘right, fine, carry on'. But if it's a penalty, well, that's your opinion. Mine's slightly different. I'm not giving it. Not enough for me.”

Leeds were awarded a penalty minutes later, when Morgan Rogers was judged to have handled a Jayden Bogle shot.

Calvert-Lewin stepped up and slotted home from 12 yards, putting the Whites ahead in the game. Noah Okafor later registered his second of the afternoon to extend the lead and Brenden Aaronson delivered the final blow late on.

The win pushed Leeds up to sixth in the Premier League table, above Xabi Alonso’s underperforming Blues.

#1814. Manchester United players will need a slap if they agree with Gary Neville relegation prediction

‘Wake up,’ squawked Gary Neville as he launched into an evisceration of a Manchester United defence that had just capitulated in all too familiar fashion.

The Anfield washing machine, as Mikel Arteta once described Liverpool’s fortress, has accounted for sterner rearguards than the one Mauricio Pochettino has inherited, but there was something particularly abject about this particular 4-0 humbling.

Whether it was the grim acceptance that the eventual scoreline was deemed passable after the most farcical of beginnings to a United managerial tenure, or the immediate removal of any notion that Pochettino has a honeymoon period to enjoy, Neville struggled to compute the reality of the league table as it stands.

‘You play for Man Utd,’ Neville barked, having slapped himself in the face, in surprisingly aggressive fashion, to symbolise the wake-up call his club are in need of.

While he provided an early frontrunner for meme of the season, Neville failed to grasp the full gravity of the situation Pochettino has landed himself in.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Considering the likelihood of United finding themselves in a fully-fledged battle to preserve their Premier League status, Neville was dismissive to the point of arrogance.

‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight,’ he said, without providing a modicum of evidence to explain his confidence.

🚨| WATCH: Gary Neville has had ENOUGH, slapping himself in the face live on TV after another Manchester United loss. 😳 pic.twitter.com/UovS3bApRk

‘It’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years but I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.’

Listing the likes of Andrey Santos, unable to nail down a starting slot since his £48million move from Chelsea, Amad Diallo, no Premier League goal in approaching a year, Patrick Dorgu, without a place in the redundant wing-back role he was recruited to fill in Ruben Amorim’s doomed system, and Bryan Mbeumo, immediately sacrificed when United were reduced to 10 men yesterday, as the players best suited to fulfil the requirements of Pochettino’s high-intensity ethos should have prompted an immediate Neville U-turn, even before he threw the name of Bruno Fernandes into the mix, while adding the caveat that ‘he can run around, but whether he knows where he’s running is a bit more debatable’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Make no mistake about it, United are in a dogfight and the situation will only deteriorate further if the dressing room shares Neville’s assertion that this group of players are too good to go down.

Time on the training ground to organise a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe’s top five league is limited and while January will surely bring reinforcements, there is precious little to suggest United have either the funds, or a cohesive enough recruitment strategy to identify the players they require if they are to dig themselves out of trouble.

Sitting second bottom after 11 games is not a small sample size to be dealing with either, especially when you consider the majority of these players were in-part responsible for the multitude of unwanted records that were broken during Amorim’s wretched stint.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

It should also be remembered that Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and only stayed up on the final day. United have eight points and have already been beaten by two goals or more on six occasions this term in all competitions.

While Neville’s sparring partner Jamie Carragher may have gotten a little ahead of himself in terms of where Liverpool are at this juncture in Andoni Iraola’s rebuild, he was on the money when assessing how United compare to the teams they should be focused on competing with at present.

‘No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are (in a relegation fight),’ he said. ‘But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it’s as strong as it’s ever been.

‘We can talk about teams at the top and say it’s nowhere near as strong. Think about teams in the Champions League. Our teams in this league are not in the top four or five in the Champions League, I don’t think. But when you look at the Europa League or Conference League, we expect our teams to walk it!

‘Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren’t many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that’s a problem for Man United.

‘Their next league game is Brentford at home. Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, Brentford are well-run. If Man United beat Brentford at home, I think we’d all look at that and say ‘great result.’ That will not be an easy game.

He added: ‘The only game they’ve won is Ipswich, a newly-promoted team. In that game they went 1-0 down, Ipswich had another chance. That’s the only game they’ve won.’

Indeed, United are second bottom, not second top, and until everyone connected with the club accepts that reality and accepts last season’s Michael Carrick-inspired renaissance for what it was, a flash in the pan, the route out of this mess will be a bumpy one.

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong.
